scope: Fixed independent Gaia candidate and optional first harmonic only; no period search.
prediction: A stable orbital or rotation-related modulation should retain a nonzero coefficient vector at the same ephemeris across independent observing epochs. A signal in one reduction or one short TESS sector alone will not establish this.
primary: ASAS-SN g, quality-valid detections, UTC-date and camera grouped medians; primary train <=2021, validation >=2022. One shared modulation with constant camera offsets and a joint continuous piecewise linear 365-day nuisance trend. Time phase zero is JD2457000. Gaussian WLS weights use max(daily propagated formal error,0.02mag); no brightness clipping.
sensitivity: 180/730day trend knots; independent observing-season intercept/slope; equal weights; sine/cosine alone versus adding first harmonic. V-band and ZTF differential g are separate diagnostics.
coherence: Report independently fit train/validation amplitude and phase and held-out SSE change when frozen training periodic coefficients are applied while validation nuisance is refit. Negative improvement weakens coherent modulation. No signal claim from training significance alone. Compare coefficient discrepancy using white-noise-only covariance, explicitly incomplete for correlated noise.
injections: At actual daily cadence inject 0.01/0.03/0.10mag semi-amplitudes at 12 uniformly spaced phases; measure paired coefficient increments through the joint nuisance/periodic model, signal energy retained after nuisance projection, and bias/phase scatter of recovered total coefficients against the real baseline. Report sensitivity relative to structured real residuals rather than formal errors alone.
tess: QUALITY==0 only, finite positive flux and errors where available; convert each sector/reduction flux to relative magnitude using its own median, daily groups. Keep QLP SAP, QLP corrected flux, SPOC SAP, SPOC PDCSAP separate. Use sector-specific offsets and slopes; 2021 vs2023 fixed-phase comparison when possible.2026 short coverage descriptive. Sector normalization is not longterm flux truth; fitting a36day period to27day sectors remains degenerate. No treating duplicate reductions as independent detections.
weakening_outcomes: Heldout signal worsens fit, phase fails to repeat, nuisance-dependent amplitude/phase, strong projection loss, disagreement of SAP/corrected light curves, or inadequate phase baseline => no established coherent photometric counterpart.
interpretation_limits: Gaia candidate fails recommended gold-sample significance/efficiency cuts. Even a matched photometric period would neither confirm a companion nor its connection to historical dimming. Fixed-period uncertainties and period/ephemeris uncertainty can reduce long-baseline phase coherence; exact Gaia period is the bounded tested hypothesis. HJD/BJD timing differences of minutes are small but not converted. No network used.
